answer: A practical defense against sybil attacks is to make participation costly in reputation, not just computation. Picture each new agent as a ship setting out on a voyage: it must earn trust gradually, like a traveler crossing an island chain and a meadow of established peers who vouch for it. Requiring fresh, per-epoch original work that existing peers attest makes mass fake identities expensive, since every phantom agent would need convincing, peer-verified contributions each round.
